evidence.title: Improvement of image quality on low-dose dynamic myocardial perfusion computed tomography with a novel 4-dimensional similarity filter
evidence.abstract: Abstract The aim of this study was to evaluate the effect of a novel 4-dimensional similarity filter (4DSF) on quantitative and qualitative parameters of low-dose dynamic myocardial computed tomography perfusion (CTP) images. In this retrospective study, medical records of 32 patients with suspected or known coronary artery disease who underwent dynamic myocardial CTP at 80 kV were included. The 4DSF reduces noise by averaging voxels that have similar dynamic behavior after adaptive iterative dose reduction 3D (AIDR3D) and deformable image registration were applied. Qualitative (artefact, contour sharpness, and myocardial homogeneity [1 = poor; 2 = intermediate; 3 = good]) and quantitative measurement (standard deviation [SD] and signal-to-noise ratio [SNR]) were compared between the 4DSF and AIDR3D. Contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR) between ischemic and normal remote myocardium was also assessed using myocardial perfusion magnetic resonance imaging as the reference standard in seven patients. The 4DSF was successfully applied to all the images. Improvement in subjective image quality yielded by 4DSF was higher than that yielded by AIDR3D (homogeneity, 1.0 [3 vs 2]; artefact, 1.5 [3 vs 1.5]; P < .001) in all patients. The 4DSF significantly decreased the SD by 59% (AIDR3D vs 4DSF: 33.5 ± 0.4 vs 13.8 ± 0.4, P < .001), increased the SNR by 134% (AIDR3D vs 4DSF: 4.4 ± 0.2 vs 10.3 ± 0.2, P < .001), and increased the CNR by 131% (AIDR3D vs 4DSF: 1.6 ± 0.2 vs 3.7 ± 0.2, P < .001). The 4DSF improved the qualitative and quantitative parameters of low-dose dynamic myocardial CTP images.

evidence.title: Data Likelihood of Active Fires Satellite Detection and Applications to Ignition Estimation and Data Assimilation
evidence.abstract: Data likelihood of fire detection is the probability of the observed detection outcome given the state of the fire spread model. We derive fire detection likelihood of satellite data as a function of the fire arrival time on the model grid. The data likelihood is constructed by a combination of the burn model, the logistic regression of the active fires detections, and the Gaussian distribution of the geolocation error. The use of the data likelihood is then demonstrated by an estimation of the ignition point of a wildland fire by the maximization of the likelihood of MODIS and VIIRS data over multiple possible ignition points.

evidence.title: A review of wildland fire spread modelling, 1990-present, 1: Physical and quasi-physical models
evidence.abstract: In recent years, advances in computational power and spatial data analysis (GIS, remote sensing, etc) have led to an increase in attempts to model the spread and behaviour of wildland fires across the landscape. This series of review papers endeavours to critically and comprehensively review all types of surface fire spread models developed since 1990. This paper reviews models of a physical or quasi-physical nature. These models are based on the fundamental chemistry and/or physics of combustion and fire spread. Other papers in the series review models of an empirical or quasi-empirical nature, and mathematical analogues and simulation models. Many models are extensions or refinements of models developed before 1990. Where this is the case, these models are also discussed but much less comprehensively.

evidence.title: The impact of domestic plug-in hybrid electric vehicles on power distribution system loads
evidence.abstract: The market for Plug-in Hybrid Electric Vehicle (PHEVs) is expected to grow significantly over the next few years and a number of new products are soon to come onto the market, such as the Toyota Prius plug-in version, . The charging demand of wide-scale use of PHEVs may have a significant impact on domestic electricity loads and could risk of overloading the power system if appropriate charging strategies not applied to prevent this. A Monte Carlo Simulation (MCS) model of domestic PHEV use and availability has been developed based on probabilistic characterisations obtained from UKTUS and quantifies charging demand of PHEVs as a function of time of day. The MCS model has been developed in order to simulate the impact on the electricity distribution system. This article also discusses the potential for responsive battery charging load from PHEVs

evidence.title: Triggering extreme events at the nanoscale in photonic seas
evidence.abstract: This work is supported by Kaust (Award No. CRG-1-2012-FRA-005), by NanoNextNL of the Dutch ministry EL&I and 130 partners and by the EU FET project ‘SPANGL4Q’.Hurricanes, tsunamis, rogue waves and tornadoes are rare natural phenomena that embed an exceptionally large amount of energy, which appears and quickly disappears in a probabilistic fashion. This makes them difficult to predict and hard to generate on demand. Here we demonstrate that we can trigger the onset of rare events akin to rogue waves controllably, and systematically use their generation to break the diffraction limit of light propagation. We illustrate this phenomenon in the case of a random field, where energy oscillates among incoherent degrees of freedom. Despite the low energy carried by each wave, we illustrate how to control a mechanism of spontaneous synchronization, which constructively builds up the spectral energy available in the whole bandwidth of the field into giant structures, whose statistics is predictable. The larger the frequency bandwidth of the random field, the larger the amplitude of rare events that are built up by this mechanism. Our system is composed of an integrated optical resonator, realized on a photonic crystal chip. Through near-field imaging experiments, we record confined rogue waves characterized by a spatial localization of 206 nm and with an ultrashort duration of 163 fs at a wavelength of 1.55 μm. Such localized energy patterns are formed in a deterministic dielectric structure that does not require nonlinear properties.Peer reviewe

We focus our attention on the case of vector field co-propagation in randomly birefringent optical fibers, and on the coupling among counter propagating waves in a periodic nonlinear waveguide

mechanism_map.intervention: Apply a 4D-similarity-filter-style algorithm to the parked Rogue's battery thermal sensor array: register each cell's temperature time series, cluster cells with similar dynamic thermal trajectories, and average within-cluster readings to denoise; cells whose trajectory deviates from all similarity clusters are flagged as anomalous hot spots, triggering a parked-vehicle alert (e.g., app notification or local alarm) independent of dashboard warning lights.
mechanism_map.expected_effect: Reduced thermal-sensor noise on parked vehicles reveals subtle, localized temperature excursions (early thermal-runaway precursors) that raw single-sensor readings mask, enabling fire-risk detection during parking without reliance on prior warning lights.

abstract.value: The market for Plug-in Hybrid Electric Vehicle (PHEVs) is expected to grow significantly over the next few years and a number of new products are soon to come onto the market, such as the Toyota Prius plug-in version, . The charging demand of wide-scale use of PHEVs may have a significant impact on domestic electricity loads and could risk of overloading the power system if appropriate charging strategies not applied to prevent this. A Monte Carlo Simulation (MCS) model of domestic PHEV use and availability has been developed based on probabilistic characterisations obtained from UKTUS and quantifies charging demand of PHEVs as a function of time of day. The MCS model has been developed in order to simulate the impact on the electricity distribution system. This article also discusses the potential for responsive battery charging load from PHEVs

warnings.mechanism: Capability collision test — keyword collision search is insufficient to establish novelty
warnings.lesson:
FROZEN THEOREM CE-018: A novelty claim survives only when the candidate's CAPABILITY (what it can DO) is demonstrably absent from the prior art landscape — not when the candidate's KEYWORDS (what words it uses) are absent. The correct procedure: (1) decompose the candidate into its functional capabilities (e.g., 'intrapprocedural clot sensing' not 'retrieved-clot physical signature measurement'); (2) search the prior art landscape for each capability using the prior art's own vocabulary (assignee names, CPC classes, commercial product names, inventor terminology); (3) build a capability collision matrix mapping each capability to prior art coverage; (4) only if at least one capability is genuinely UNOCCUPIED (confirmed by both patent search AND commercial frontier analysis) can a novelty claim be recorded. Semantic re-skins (CE-012 violation) include: 'retrieved-clot' vs 'in-situ clot'; 'physical signature' vs 'composition'; 'integrated sensor' vs 'catheter-mounted sensor.' These distinctions prove nothing. The test is capability, not vocabulary.

SHARPENED (per CEO Round 62 audit): Capability novelty must be evaluated at the FUNCTIONAL END-TO-END level: input → inference → decision → physical effect → measurable outcome. Otherwise the machine can still find a 'novel' intermediate layer (e.g., a new sensor modality, a new feature, a new algorithm) that is already covered by an existing end-to-end system. The correct end-to-end test: (5) decompose the candidate into the complete causal loop — what is observed → what is inferred → what is predicted → what physical action becomes possible → what measurable outcome changes; (6) map each step of this loop to the prior art's end-to-end systems (not just individual capabilities); (7) only if the candidate's complete causal loop is demonstrably absent from the prior art's end-to-end systems can a novelty claim be recorded. A 'novel' intermediate layer that plugs into an existing end-to-end system is NOT novel — it is a substitution, not an invention. The unit of novelty is the complete causal loop, not the sensor, feature, algorithm, or capability.

informational.mechanism: RES-4 narrow: adaptive transverse/sigmoid sinus stent for CSF absorption regulation via AG pressure gradient control
informational.lesson: MODEL-BOUNDED NEGATIVE RESULT: Before inventing variable geometry, calculate absolute pressure-control authority at the actual operating point. Relative r^4 sensitivity is meaningless if the absolute pressure drop is tiny. Under realistic post-stenting conditions (D=5-10mm, Q=200-500 mL/min), adaptive diameter control of a venous sinus produces <0.2 mmHg change in AG gradient — 5x below the 1 mmHg pre-registered threshold. Control authority exists only in the stenotic+high-flow regime (D≤4mm, Q≥1200 mL/min), which is incompatible with a stented patient whose stent has normalized diameter to 7-10mm. The network model (1323 configs) confirms: flow redistribution through contralateral sinus does NOT rescue control authority (dominance has no effect). NOT a universal vascular invariant — based on Poiseuille model with specific assumptions about geometry, flow, and topology.

informational.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-019: A clinical-pathway-aware evidence selector must demonstrate that the clinical-pathway bridge produces a MATERIALLY DIFFERENT and BETTER evidence set than information-maximizing selection (BOED). If the pathway-aware selector uses MORE tests while achieving WORSE assurance, the clinical-pathway bridge adds complexity without value. The minimum-evidence claim must be validated by showing tests_required < BOED, not just tests_required < conventional. The killer experiment must compare against the STRONGEST available baseline (BOED), not just conventional full-validation.

informational.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-020: A sufficiency proof that is merely an integration of known statistical methods (NI testing + coverage + multiple-testing correction + sensitivity analysis) is NOT a novel mathematical result. Under §103, combining known methods to solve a problem the market explicitly asks for is likely obvious (KSR v. Teleflex). The frontier is a NEW MATHEMATICAL BOUND — e.g., a tight bound on minimum evidence set size that is better than what existing methods give individually, or a proof technique that connects clinical pathway coverage to statistical sufficiency in a way that is not derivable from existing theory. Additionally: killer tests for sufficiency proofs must include a TRUE POSITIVE case (sufficient evidence for a SAFE modification that the system correctly accepts), not just a true negative (insufficient evidence that the system correctly rejects).

Under KSR, combining known methods to solve a problem the market explicitly asks for is obvious. informational.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-022: Synergy ≠ novelty and synergy ≠ commercial moat. A functional interaction (A changes B) is NECESSARY but NOT SUFFICIENT for invention. The interaction itself — the causal law, the emergent effect, and functional equivalents across domains — must survive prior art independently. Additionally: synergy claims without quantitative comparison against the STRONGEST baseline are stories, not evidence. The unexpected-effect proof requires: (1) pre-registered quantitative prediction, (2) strongest baseline identified, (3) killer experiment vs that baseline, (4) result not predictable from A and B independently. The new standard: A changes B → unexpected effect → interaction survives prior art → reproducible advantage → cannot be cheaply reproduced → buyer value.

informational.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-023: A candidate that survives the 14-gate protocol at the CONCEPT level can be killed at the ELEMENT-DECOMPOSITION level. The 14 gates assessed M4 against the broad concept (continuously renewing anti-biofilm surface) and found M4=NOT FOUND. But deep collision revealed that each element (continuous renewal, dynamic topography, surface-energy modulation) is individually occupied by prior art. The combination is an aggregation of known anti-fouling approaches. The lesson: M4 must be assessed at the ELEMENT level, not the concept level. And M4=NOT FOUND means the search has not found comparable performance yet — not that it does not exist.

custody_records.raw_content: Abstract The aim of this study was to evaluate the effect of a novel 4-dimensional similarity filter (4DSF) on quantitative and qualitative parameters of low-dose dynamic myocardial computed tomography perfusion (CTP) images. In this retrospective study, medical records of 32 patients with suspected or known coronary artery disease who underwent dynamic myocardial CTP at 80 kV were included. The 4DSF reduces noise by averaging voxels that have similar dynamic behavior after adaptive iterative dose reduction 3D (AIDR3D) and deformable image registration were applied. Qualitative (artefact, contour sharpness, and myocardial homogeneity [1 = poor; 2 = intermediate; 3 = good]) and quantitative measurement (standard deviation [SD] and signal-to-noise ratio [SNR]) were compared between the 4DSF and AIDR3D. Contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR) between ischemic and normal remote myocardium was also assessed using myocardial perfusion magnetic resonance imaging as the reference standard in seven patients. The 4DSF was successfully applied to all the images. Improvement in subjective image quality yielded by 4DSF was higher than that yielded by AIDR3D (homogeneity, 1.0 [3 vs 2]; artefact, 1.5 [3 vs 1.5]; P < .001) in all patients. The 4DSF significantly decreased the SD by 59% (AIDR3D vs 4DSF: 33.5 ± 0.4 vs 13.8 ± 0.4, P < .001), increased the SNR by 134% (AIDR3D vs 4DSF: 4.4 ± 0.2 vs 10.3 ± 0.2, P < .001), and increased the CNR by 131% (AIDR3D vs 4DSF: 1.6 ± 0.2 vs 3.7 ± 0.2, P < .001). The 4DSF improved the qualitative and quantitative parameters of low-dose dynamic myocardial CTP images.

We derive fire detection likelihood of satellite data as a function of the fire arrival time on the model grid. The data likelihood is constructed by a combination of the burn model, the logistic regression of the active fires detections, and the Gaussian distribution of the geolocation error. The use of the data likelihood is then demonstrated by an estimation of the ignition point of a wildland fire by the maximization of the likelihood of MODIS and VIIRS data over multiple possible ignition points.

custody_records.raw_content: In recent years, advances in computational power and spatial data analysis (GIS, remote sensing, etc) have led to an increase in attempts to model the spread and behaviour of wildland fires across the landscape. This series of review papers endeavours to critically and comprehensively review all types of surface fire spread models developed since 1990. This paper reviews models of a physical or quasi-physical nature. These models are based on the fundamental chemistry and/or physics of combustion and fire spread. Other papers in the series review models of an empirical or quasi-empirical nature, and mathematical analogues and simulation models. Many models are extensions or refinements of models developed before 1990. Where this is the case, these models are also discussed but much less comprehensively.

The charging demand of wide-scale use of PHEVs may have a significant impact on domestic electricity loads and could risk of overloading the power system if appropriate charging strategies not applied to prevent this. A Monte Carlo Simulation (MCS) model of domestic PHEV use and availability has been developed based on probabilistic characterisations obtained from UKTUS and quantifies charging demand of PHEVs as a function of time of day. The MCS model has been developed in order to simulate the impact on the electricity distribution system. This article also discusses the potential for responsive battery charging load from PHEVs

This makes them difficult to predict and hard to generate on demand. Here we demonstrate that we can trigger the onset of rare events akin to rogue waves controllably, and systematically use their generation to break the diffraction limit of light propagation. We illustrate this phenomenon in the case of a random field, where energy oscillates among incoherent degrees of freedom. The larger the frequency bandwidth of the random field, the larger the amplitude of rare events that are built up by this mechanism. Our system is composed of an integrated optical resonator, realized on a photonic crystal chip. Through near-field imaging experiments, we record confined rogue waves characterized by a spatial localization of 206 nm and with an ultrashort duration of 163 fs at a wavelength of 1.55 μm.
